plan: Sell SOXL and SPAL to zero to eliminate all leveraged ETF exposure.
Trim SPY to 20% to reduce concentration and cure the mandate breach.
Add to QQQI, targeting 25% of the book, to favor income and stability.

conservative.read: This conservative plan targets around 1.5% per month, focusing on capital preservation. It significantly reduces risk by eliminating leveraged ETFs and lowering concentration. Expect lower volatility and drawdowns, but also more modest returns.

plan: Trim SOXL to 3% and SPAL to 2% to reduce leveraged ETF exposure.
Reduce SPY to 25% to cure the concentration breach.
Buy TECL, a strong scanner setup, for 4% of the book.
Add to CRWD, increasing its allocation to 16%, for quality tech exposure.
This plan balances risk and growth, maintaining a small leveraged ETF presence.
balanced.read: This balanced plan aims for approximately 2.5% per month, prioritizing risk-first growth. It reduces overall leverage and concentration while maintaining some exposure to quality tech and strong scanner setups. Expect moderate volatility and drawdowns.

plan: Trim SPY to 25% to cure the concentration breach.
Add to SOXL, increasing its allocation to 6%, leaning into leveraged semiconductors.
Add to SPAL, increasing its allocation to 6%, for leveraged space exposure.
Buy TECL, a strong scanner setup, for 6% of the book.
Increase CRWD to 18%, concentrating in a high-scoring tech name.

aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets around 4% per month, aiming for stretch growth. It significantly increases exposure to leveraged ETFs and concentrates in high-scoring setups. Be aware of substantially higher volatility, potential for larger drawdowns, and the daily decay/rebalancing of leveraged ETFs.

plan: Sell SOXL and SPAL to zero, eliminating all high-beta leveraged exposure.
Trim SPY to 20% to reduce concentration and cure the mandate breach.
Add to QQQI, targeting 30% of the book, to prioritize income for yield.
Trim QQQ to 10%, reducing growth exposure in favor of income.

income.read: This income plan targets around 1% per month, focusing on parking cash for yield. It prioritizes low drawdown and reliable income over growth by rotating into income/covered-call ETFs. Remember, distributions are variable and NAV can still fall in a selloff.
